clue.text: NEWS, as stuck in pupils’ jotters?

definitions.text: NEWS, as stuck in pupils’ jotters?

blocks.note: surface reading: the day's news, written up in schoolchildren's exercise books
setter's reading: N, E, W and S are the four cardinal directions, and a geometry set's drawing tool has a sharp tip that gets jabbed into school notebooks

explanation.surface: Pupils writing up the day's news in their school exercise books.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWS spells the four directions North, East, West, South; COMPASS POINTS are also the sharp ends of the drawing compasses a pupil sticks into a jotter (a Scottish word for an exercise book).
explanation.definitionFit: North, East, West and South are the cardinal bearings marked on a navigational dial, and the pupil's geometry tool also has pointed tips.

clue.text: Old Greek character has little hesitation producing drug

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
um is the short noise of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek figure barely hesitates before turning out a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is a narcotic made from poppy sap, so it is a straightforward example of a drug.

clue.text: End of the Footsie, whether in the market-place or at home?

definitions.text: End of the Footsie, whether in the market-place or at home?

blocks.clueFragment: End of the Footsie, whether in the market-place
blocks.note: surface reading: the close of trading on the FTSE share index, nicknamed the Footsie, in the financial markets
setter's reading: the ends of the feet are toes, and the nursery rhyme has one little toe going to market and another staying at home

explanation.surface: The close of trading on the London stock index, whether on the trading floor or watched from home.
explanation.walkthrough: The Footsie is the FTSE 100, the London share index, but here it is the foot; the rhyme 'This little piggy went to market, this little piggy stayed home' is counted on a child's toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Piggies is a nursery word for toes, which sit at the far end of a foot, from the children's counting rhyme.

clue.text: Thin wooden poles seen with last of wreckage

indicators.note: last of asks for only the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: spars are stout poles, as used for masts
the final letter of wreckage

explanation.surface: Thin wooden poles lie among the remains of a shipwreck.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered, so it matches thin in the sense of meagre or scanty in number.

clue.text: Advance completed, opponent offering no resistance

blocks.note: a push is an advance, as by an army
something over is finished

explanation.surface: An army's advance is finished because the enemy put up no fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushover is someone easily beaten or persuaded, an adversary who puts up no fight at all.

clue.text: Sign first

blocks.note: first meaning: to mark a document with one's abbreviated name
second meaning: occurring at the beginning

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to sign before anything else, but each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to mark a paper with abbreviated letters of one's name; as an adjective it means at the very beginning.

clue.text: They're willing to leave

blocks.note: surface reading: people who are happy and ready to depart
setter's reading: people making a will in order to bequeath their property

explanation.surface: Some people are perfectly ready to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is someone who has made a legal will, so they are literally 'willing' estates and belongings to heirs.

clue.text: Bug making arm go crimson, | suspect

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious and not to be taken in its given form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters as written, the bar being the printed pronoun I

explanation.surface: Someone suspects an insect bite is turning their arm red.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan's vertical bar is the capital I, which supplies the second I the anagram needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bug is an informal word for a germ or microbe, a tiny living thing seen only under a microscope.

clue.text: Maestro with only half a baton?

definitions.text: Maestro with only half a baton?

blocks.note: surface reading: an orchestra leader whose stick has snapped
setter's reading: someone only half doing the job of leading an orchestra, a 'half' version of the role

explanation.surface: An orchestra leader is left waving a broken stick.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a half conductor; the real thing is a material such as silicon used in electronics.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicon and similar materials pass electric current only partly, between metals and insulators, hence a 'half' version of a current carrier.

clue.text: Mica is in a see-through container

blocks.note: taken as written
a glass is a transparent drinking vessel

explanation.surface: A sample of mineral is kept in a clear jar.
explanation.definitionFit: Isinglass is an old name for thin transparent sheets of the mineral mica, once used in stove windows.

clue.text: Children’s publication

blocks.note: first meaning: a person's offspring
second meaning: one edition of a magazine or the act of putting something out

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a children's magazine, but the possessive is just the join between two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal language offspring are called someone's descendants or progeny; separately, an edition of a periodical is one number put out.

clue.text: Stays - ie controls, holding Mother in?

indicators.note: holding means gripping and enclosing, so the controls wrap around another piece
in confirms that Mother ends up placed inside rather than beside

blocks.note: reins are the straps used to control a horse
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone stays put, that is, keeps Mother indoors under tight control.
explanation.definitionFit: Remains as a verb means stays or continues to be in place, a direct synonym in the third person.

clue.text: Japanese art originally shown by Parisian friend

blocks.note: ORIG is the dictionary abbreviation for originally
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A French friend first showed someone a craft from Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' looks like an instruction to take a first letter, but here it is shortened as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the traditional Japanese craft of folding paper into decorative shapes, so it is an example of such an art.

clue.text: Does as ordered in Black Sea port

indicators.note: ordered means arranged or set out anew, so the letters take a fresh sequence

blocks.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone obeys instructions in a harbour city on the Black Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Ukrainian harbour city on the northern coast of that inland sea.

clue.text: He's ill, but contrived to install decoration and ornament

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially put together, so the letters are rearranged
to install something is to set it inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: the letters as written
the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: A sick man still manages to put up decorations and ornaments.
explanation.walkthrough: The MBE is a British state honour, worn as a medal, hence a decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish is to adorn or beautify, which is what to ornament means as a verb.

clue.text: It's a bore to attend to - that’s rich!

blocks.note: a bore is a hole drilled for water or oil
taken as written
to do a task is to attend to it

explanation.surface: Someone protests that being told a tedious chore must be dealt with is a bit much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's rich!' sounds like an indignant exclamation, but rich is the definition; a bore is a drilled hole, not a dull person.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do describes people who are prosperous and comfortably off, which is what wealthy or affluent means.

clue.text: Sea creature, terribly scary if handled, initially

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly mangled, so these letters are jumbled
initially points to only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the letters as written
the first letter of handled

explanation.surface: A sea creature that is frightening if you pick it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayfish is a lobster-like crustacean; the sea variety is the spiny lobster, so it is a marine animal.

clue.text: Attend meeting with foe or beg to differ

indicators.note: to differ is to become unlike the original, so the letters change their order

blocks.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone at a meeting with an enemy can either plead or disagree.
explanation.definitionFit: To go before a panel or court is to appear in front of it, attending a hearing with its members.

clue.text: Waste food that's been fried

blocks.note: first meaning: to squander
second meaning: a piece of food dipped in batter and cooked in hot fat

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as leftover fried food, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to squander time or money bit by bit; as a noun it is a battered piece of fruit or meat.

clue.text: Application to get in brick carrier is accommodated

indicators.note: to get in means to go inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks
application in the sense of use, as in 'practical application'

explanation.surface: A form must be submitted for a builder's carrying trough to be given a home.
explanation.definitionFit: To be housed is to be given lodging or a place to live, the same as being accommodated.

clue.text: Superior US agent, exceptionally well-nourished

blocks.note: over means above or higher in rank
a fed is American slang for an FBI agent

explanation.surface: A senior American government agent is unusually well fed.
explanation.definitionFit: Overfed means given more food than is needed, so beyond the normal level of nourishment.

clue.text: Greek character on ocean taking a bout of sickness

indicators.note: taking means taking in or absorbing, so something goes inside

blocks.note: nu is the Greek letter N
taken as written
sea is a synonym for ocean

explanation.surface: A Greek sailor on the ocean has a fit of seasickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bout of' looks like part of the definition, but the A is the letter that goes inside the Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is the queasy feeling of wanting to vomit, which is what sickness means here.

clue.text: Make invalid have fun dancing with Lily

indicators.note: dancing suggests moving around, so the letters shift into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invalid is urged to enjoy themselves dancing with a girl called Lily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' reads as a sick person, but here it is the adjective, stressed on the second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: To nullify is to cancel or void something legally, making it no longer valid.

clue.text: Minced lamb with bits of ice? Still...

indicators.note: minced meat is chopped up small, so these letters are cut up and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dish of minced lamb is served with ice chips, and that's still not all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like the adverb trailing off, but it is the noun: a distilling apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: An alembic is an old distilling vessel used by alchemists, and a still is apparatus for distillation.

clue.text: Pig-meat firm restricted by embargo

indicators.note: restricted by means hemmed in on both sides, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: an embargo is an official ban on trade
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A pork company's business is hampered by a trade embargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is cured meat from the back or sides of a pig, so it is one kind of pork product.

clue.text: Remove garment

blocks.note: first meaning: to move something from its place
second meaning: a straight loose dress or undergarment

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to take off clothing, but the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to move or displace something; as a noun it is a simple loose dress or chemise.

clue.text: Coat fop is wearing, necessarily so

indicators.note: wearing in the sense of wearing away or fraying, so the letters are worn out of shape

blocks.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A dandy in a coat, of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' suggests a container with the fop dressed in the coat, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipso facto is Latin for 'by that very fact', meaning something follows automatically, as a necessary consequence.

clue.text: Dreadful crunch drew ash from tobacco-pipes

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something in a terrible state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A horrible crunching sound comes as ash is drawn from pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay smoking pipe, named after the parish officials said to favour them.
